rv.q: Stereophonic is hugely engrossing and enjoyable, but like the band’s album, it could lose a few fiddly bits and a few minutes.
We shouldn’t really watch – but we can’t look away.
While the balance between art and heart-ache, technical challenge and emotional clash, is well achieved, what’s missing are the specifics that might give the band a stronger inner-life.
Personally, I often wished Adjmi’s play were as sharply succinct. But it’s still richly evocative, and well worth a look and a listen.
rich slice of creative life delivered by a 1970s rock band
At the close, there is just the music, swirling out across the theatre, asking its own questions about the price of art, the value of love. It’s terrific.
Stereophonic is a fascinating, if flawed, meditation on the creative process.
